question: Spike planted default B Site Ascent, 2v2, 34s. You're Killjoy with 2 Nanoswarms and an Alarmbot. Your teammate holds CT Mid. How do you play post-plant?

options.label: Set both Nanoswarms on a lineup covering the default plant, then reposition in a crossfire off-angle with your teammate
options.explication_courte: Nanoswarm lineups make defusing impossible without clearing the molly spots first, forcing defenders to expose themselves; the off-spike crossfire punishes any retaker who steps up.

options.label: Hold the Nanoswarms and play a disciplined close crossfire near the spike to instantly trade the first retaker
options.explication_courte: A disciplined crossfire can win post-plants without util, but holding the mollys wastes your best delay tool; playable if your positions are well offset and on distinct lines.

sources_option.citation: Crossfires are the most consistent ranked post-plant win condition because they don't require fancy utility, just two players at distinct angles.

options.label: Throw both Nanoswarms as soon as defenders enter site — no lineup, just eyeballing it
options.explication_courte: Without a lineup, Nanoswarms often miss the exact defuse spot and get burned early; you lose your most reliable delay tool for the post-plant.

sources_option.citation: Playing for lineups is a core post-plant rule; molly lineups on the spike are hard to counter and eat up a lot of the enemies' time versus a wasted eyeballed throw.

options.label: Stack both players at the same angle near the spike for concentrated fire on the main entry
options.explication_courte: Stacking the same angle gives defenders a single line to work with — one flash or a grouped push takes you both out, and nobody covers the second defuse axis.

sources_option.citation: Spread out, don't stack the same spot; a crossfire needs two distinct angles so the defenders can't clear both of you with one utility or one push.

explication_longue:
Situation: 2v2 post-plant on B Site Ascent, default plant, 34 seconds. You're Killjoy with 2 Nanoswarms and an Alarmbot; your teammate holds CT Mid. Two defenders will attempt the retake.

Post-plant on attack rests on three levers: (1) playing for util lineups that make defusing impossible without clearing, (2) spreading players across distinct angles (never stack), (3) holding an off-spike crossfire that punishes anyone stepping up to defuse. Killjoy is the ideal post-plant agent: her Nanoswarm lineups on the default plant turn the spike into a kill zone.

The optimal line combines all three: two Nanoswarms pre-aimed at the defuse spot (activate on the defuse sound), then reposition so you and your CT teammate cover two different angles. A defender who starts defusing eats a molly; if they wait, the timer works for you. A pure crossfire (acceptable option) also wins plenty of rounds but forgoes the most reliable delay tool.

Estimated elite distribution: ~57% play lineup+off-angle crossfire, ~23% play a disciplined crossfire holding the mollys, ~15% eyeball-throw the mollys (less reliable), ~5% stack the same angle (the mistake that gives defenders a single contact point). GTO tolerance: any line that uses the lineups OR holds a crossfire at two distinct angles is solid; stacking is the only real error.

sources.citation: Playing for lineups is a core post-plant rule and the go-to since it became meta; lineups are hard to counter and eat up a lot of the enemies' time.
Attack post-plant means spreading out (not all same spot), playing off the spike, holding crossfires, and using utility to delay the defuse.
Your crossfire should cover the spike's approach lines with two players at distinct entry angles, not stacked in the same corner.

_gaps.incertitude: Estimations depuis guides post-plant (cheatspulse, dignitas, boostroom) ; la frequence exacte lineup vs crossfire-pur varie selon la maitrise des lineups Killjoy du joueur (skill-dependent).
Le crossfire agressif (option 1) pourrait etre juge equivalent a l'optimal par des joueurs qui privilegient le trade instantane ; la marge optimal/acceptable est fine.
